source.title: Using the Diffusion Model to Explain Cognitive Deficits in Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder

confidence_rationale: The most direct external challenge to MECH-080's arm 1. The claim attributes ADHD to a truncation set-point -- an urgency threshold set too low, producing premature commitment. The best-powered diffusion-model work localises ADHD's deficit to DRIFT RATE (evidence-accumulation efficiency), not boundary separation, in a well-powered sample (N=97 ADHD / 39 control) by the authors who built the model. Drift rate is a competence parameter, which places arm 1 squarely inside MECH-080's own 'reduces to lost competence' falsifier. Held at 0.70 rather than higher because a go/no-go task has no multi-step rollout at all, so the mapping is to REE's commit threshold rather than to rollout depth.
failure_signatures: ADHD's diffusion-model signature was reduced drift rate to no-go decisions, not lowered boundary separation -- if premature commitment in ADHD is an accumulation-QUALITY deficit rather than a THRESHOLD setting, MECH-080's arm 1 is mis-specified at the parameter level.

ADHD children showed an INCREASED starting point (bias toward responding) alongside reduced drift, so the observed prematurity is jointly produced by bias and poor accumulation -- a REE manipulation of rollout_horizon alone cannot reproduce this and a match on behaviour would be a false positive.

Because drift rate IS competence, any REE result in which a shortened rollout_horizon produces premature harmful commits is indistinguishable from the conversion-ceiling competence artefact that MECH-080's own precondition rules out as uninformative.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In 97 children with ADHD and 39 controls aged 8-10 performing go/no-go tasks at varying event rates, diffusion-model decomposition attributed ADHD's higher rate of failed inhibitions to a reduced drift rate toward no-go decisions at faster event rates, alongside an increased starting point, rather than to a lowered decision boundary.
mapping.ree_translation: Directly contests MECH-080's arm-1 parameterisation. The claim reads ADHD as a BG urgency threshold set too low -- in REE terms a lowered commit threshold or a shortened rollout, both of which are policy settings that leave the underlying model intact. This paper says the ADHD signature is instead degraded evidence quality, which in REE maps to a worse z_world / E1-E2 readout rather than to any truncation set-point.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A go/no-go task involves a single-step decision with no forward rollout whatsoever, so the boundary parameter here is an analog of REE's E3 commit threshold and NOT of config.e2.rollout_horizon. The paper cannot adjudicate rollout DEPTH directly; what it adjudicates is whether ADHD's prematurity is a threshold phenomenon at all, which is the prior question MECH-080's arm 1 assumes an answer to. Children aged 8-10 to a REE agent is a further and substantial step.
mapping.source_context: Children aged 8-10, ADHD (N=97, 33 girls) vs control (N=39, 26 girls); go/no-go tasks across manipulated event rates; Ratcliff diffusion model decomposition.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high: Ratcliff and McKoon are the diffusion model's authors, N is well above typical for the design, and the event-rate manipulation is the right way to stress the parameter separation. Mapping fidelity 0.60 -- the threshold-vs-drift distinction transfers cleanly to REE, the single-step task limits inference about rollout depth. Transfer risk 0.40 for the paediatric-to-agent step.
